subcategory: nugget-augmented generation with citation provenance for report generation
task: Citation-supported report generation over multilingual collections (TREC NeuCLIR)
problem: Long-form RAG reports repeat information and lose citation provenance when content is clustered or summarised; nugget-based ideas are used for evaluation but not to drive generation.
architecture: Crucible: builds a bank of top-20 Q&A nuggets per request from retrieved documents (with paraphrase-based quality ranking), scans document chunks for passages answering each nugget and extracts one self-contained sentence with confidence, optionally verifies coverage and citation support with AutoArgue-style LLM prompts, and assembles a report where every sentence cites exactly one document.
retriever: PLAID-X multilingual dense retriever (also Qwen3 embeddings and MILCO)
knowledge_source: TREC NeuCLIR 2024 multilingual news collection (machine-translated to English)

datasets.name: TREC NeuCLIR 2024 Report Generation Pilot
datasets.details: topic-focused report requests with gold nugget banks

key_results: Crucible-Base nugget recall 0.584 vs 0.230 for Ginger and 0.177 for GptResearcher.
Verification raises citation support from 0.595 to 0.932 and nugget density from 0.392 to 0.495.
strengths: Shows how evaluation units (nuggets) can control redundancy and keep per-sentence provenance.
Reports variants with and without the verification step to expose evaluator leakage.

limitations.text: Developed with organisers of NeuCLIR and AutoArgue; the verification step is circular with the AutoArgue evaluator and may inflate citation support.
Designed for quality, not speed: LLM calls scale quadratically for paraphrase detection and with nuggets x documents for scanning.

notes: Read from the arXiv copy of the ECIR 2026 paper.
title: Incorporating Q&A Nuggets Into Retrieval-Augmented Generation
read_from: arXiv preprint 2601.13222 (open-access copy; citation uses the published version)
